title: Properties of the stable cube weights
statement: Let $n\\in\\mathbb N$ and $-1\\le\\rho\\le1$. On the Boolean cube $\\{0,1\\}^n$, assign the ordered pair $(x,y)$ weight $W(x,y)=2^{-n}\\prod_{i=1}^n(1+\\rho\\sigma(x_i)\\sigma(y_i))/2$, where $\\sigma(0)=1$ and $\\sigma(1)=-1$. These weights are nonnegative and symmetric, each row sums to $2^{-n}$, and the sum over all ordered pairs is one.
replaced: Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $-1\le\rho\le1$, and put $W(x,y)=2^{-n}\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}[(1+\rho(-1)^{x_i+y_i})/2]$ for cube points $x,y$. Then $W(x,y)\ge0$, $W(x,y)=W(y,x)$, $\sum_yW(x,y)=2^{-n}$ for every $x$, and $\sum_{x,y}W(x,y)=1$.
